brief: Solves and draws a mathematical diagram: objects and relations laid out so that every rule about them holds.
detail: A diagram is made of three parts: a domain (set theory, geometry, graphs), a substance that declares the objects and asserts relations between them, and a style that turns each object into shapes and each relation into rules. Nothing is drawn by hand. The first question asked of the diagram solves it, a contradictory substance gives a picture that says it is not lawful instead of an error, and every shape, number and mark can be read back, which is what lets a caption quote the picture. The figure can be pinned, dragged, windowed, marked and written out as SVG or PNG.
receiver: os = new stzMathSubstance(StzSetTheoryDomain()); os.DeclareAll("Set", [ "A", "B" ]); os.Assert("Subset", [ "B", "A" ]); os.AutoLabelAll(); o1 = new stzMathDiagram(StzSetTheoryDomain(), os, StzEulerStyle())
